rationale: With one turn left and no room for a new execution, I recorded a branch of the verify path that the existing account leaves implicit: VerifyLeader answers success immediately, with no peer contact and no heartbeat, whenever the configuration's voter quorum size is one. That bounds the non-voter acknowledgement defect the account asserts - it needs a quorum larger than one - and it is the only shape of a VerifyLeader success that is decided purely from local state. The behavior entry cites the fast path's own range and the three anchors the verify account already uses.

knowledge.statement: VerifyLeader answers success without contacting any peer when the leader's voter quorum size is one. The dispatcher counts the leader's own vote, reads the quorum size from the configuration, and if that size is one it responds success and returns before it registers the request on any replication stream or triggers a heartbeat; only past that check does it track the request on every replication stream in leader state and have each stream heartbeat immediately. A configuration with a single voter, whatever non-voters accompany it, therefore gets a success that reflects only the leader's own state.
knowledge.conditions: Leader on the main thread dispatching a VerifyLeader request whose latest configuration yields a voter quorum size of one, as in a one-voter cluster with any number of non-voters; the fast path is a local check and involves no peer round trip.
